Ashwin R: Quick dump — ran a microprofile for the fused-attn branch with QKV packing + bias/rope epilogue. Seeing a perf regression when KV cache is enabled for short sequences (L<=64). Anyone seen this?
Maria G: Can you paste the numbers and the run config?
Ashwin R: Sure — baseline (flashattn-v2, no epilogue fusion): L=32, B=8, tokens/sec=43k, p99 latency per token ~0.92ms. New fused-qkv+epilogue: tokens/sec=38k, p99=1.3ms with cache=true. Without cache it's slightly better: 47k, p99=0.78ms.
Jean L: Interesting. Means epilogue path interacts badly with KV writes. I ran a profiler — kernel launch counts up ~3x when cache enabled.
Jean L: snippet:
```
Kernel: fused_attention_epilogue_qkv_pack
launches: 2400
avg_time: 0.45ms
KV_write kernels: 1200, avg 0.18ms
memory_copies: 2 per step
```
Li W: That smells like non-coalesced KV updates. If epilogue does per-head writes separately we lose memory bandwidth, and for small L the overhead dominates.
Sam T: Could also be cache invalidation on the output buffer; maybe we produce a new tensor each step instead of in-place update. Do we have the epilogue doing elementwise metadata updates?
Ashwin R: I dug into the kernel — we do atomic adds for cache pointers when rope/bias fused, introduced in PR #482. On Ampere this serializes some warps.
Maria G: Any quick fix options? Fallback to previous kernel for cached path? Or change batching heuristics to hide latencies?
Eva P: For short sequences, batching helps but introduces extra latency for first token. For interactive use we'd rather keep per-token latency low. Fallback is fine as an interim. Also epilogue fusion seems to hamper nested caching path; we can gate it behind a runtime flag and a kernel chooser rule: if cache_enabled && seq<=64 -> prefer legacy-attn.
Ashwin R: Proposed quick plan:
- Add runtime flag RUNTIME_FUSED_EPI=1/0 to enable/disable epilogue fusion.
- Update kernel chooser: if cache && seq<=64 && batch_per_device<=16 -> pick legacy QKV kernel.
- Meanwhile, Li + Jean investigate making KV writes coalesced or use per-block staging buffer.
- Canary rollout to 10% dedicated capacity.
Jean L: I also have a potential micro-optimization: pack KV in row-major order that matches GPU memory access for writes; that should drop KV_write avg from 0.18ms -> ~0.06ms in my local sim. Need real device runs.
Li W: I'll prototype per-block staging (shared mem accum + one coalesced global write). If we can avoid atomics that should remove warp serialization.
Sam T: Batching heuristic note: we should avoid automatically increasing batch size for cached flows; it hides perf regressions. Add metric to console: token-latency-by-cache-flag.
Ashwin R: Can someone run a canary with RUNTIME_FUSED_EPI=0 on dedicated pool and record p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and kernel-launch-count?
deploy-bot: Canary job scheduled -> canary-id=ci-1822, pool=dedicated-gpu-3, rollout=10%, start=2026-07-21T14:05Z :rocket:
Maria G: I'll own the canary measurement. Will post numbers in this thread.
Eva P: If fallback proves OK, we ship that as a patch. But keep the fused epilogue branch in feature flag so we can continue optimization.
Jean L: Agreed. Also adding perf tests to the nightly perf suite: small-seq cached scenarios + kernel-launch-count delta.
Ashwin R: Thanks — Li/Jean handle kernel change, Maria runs canary, Sam updates console metric. We'll regroup after results. :thumbsup:
Maria G: Canary results (first pass): legacy path w/ cache: p99 0.95ms, tokens/sec 44.5k. fused-epilogue enabled: p99 1.29ms, tokens/sec 38.2k. kernel launches +2.6x.
Li W: Got a local patch; shared-mem staging reduces KV writes and in local device: fused-epilogue + staging: p99 0.82ms, tokens/sec 46k. Pushing PR for review.
Ashwin R: Great. Let's keep the feature flag off by default until staging PR lands and we have canary green.
Sam T: I'll add the kernel-chooser rule and metric today.
Eva P: Nice progress. Tagging this for release note: "Fix: fused-attn epilogue cache write regression (patch gated)" once merged.
Ashwin R: Closing loop — next update in this thread when PR lands or canary changes. Thanks all.
